A1.justification: Both PDFs describe RoadBench. Their main text, tables, figures, and complete appendices are readable, and retained content can be matched despite extensive layout changes. Internal numerical inconsistencies limit particular interpretations but do not prevent comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original evaluations of 14 MLLMs, reference-line prompting experiments, environmental-condition analyses, and failure cases in Section 4 and Appendices 7–9.

after.justification: v2 reports original evaluations of 20 base models, three fine-tuned variants, new cross-view tasks, and repeated-evaluation statistics, alongside the retained analyses.

M1.justification: The work remains a benchmark without a proposed predictive architecture, loss, or new inference algorithm. Cross-view inputs define additional evaluation tasks, while Qwen3-VL fine-tuning is introduced as a comparison experiment.

E1.justification: v2 adds Cross-View Lane Counting and Cross-View Lane Designation Recognition, requiring joint reasoning over geographically paired BEV and FPV images. These introduce substantially different input requirements beyond v1's six separate-view tasks. The newly specified five-city provenance does not establish a geographic coverage change.

E2.justification: Table 2 adds six Qwen3-VL variants: 2B, 4B, 8B, 32B, 30B-A3B, and 235B-A22B, plus fine-tuned 2B/4B/8B variants. The original 14 models and simple baselines remain in the retained-task comparisons. Missing entries concern some models on the newly introduced cross-view tasks.

E3.justification: Reported test cases decrease from 9,121 to 3,040. Figure 2 changes BEV counting from 2,908 to 969 cases and FPV counting from 737 to 115, for example. v2 also introduces paired-image testing and training-set fine-tuning, and removes composite rank aggregation. The sampling transition, training split, and tuning budget are not specified.

E4.justification: Table 2 and Section 4.2 add an across-task comparison of untuned and fine-tuned Qwen3-VL-2B/4B/8B, examining whether task-specific training addresses benchmark weaknesses. The original prompting ablations, lighting/occlusion analyses, and six sets of detailed failure cases remain; their relocation does not constitute new analyses.

E5.justification: v1 provides no repeated-run uncertainty reporting. v2 adds Appendix 7.9 and Table 7-9, reporting means and standard deviations over three repeated evaluations for Gemini-Pro and GPT-5-Mini on FPV lane designation and both cross-view tasks. Most benchmark results remain point estimates.

E6.justification: Scores throughout the retained experiments change, and cross-view, Qwen3-VL, fine-tuning, and uncertainty result entries are added. For example, GPT-5-Mini BEV counting F1 changes from 0.3693 to 0.3550 under revised sample counts, so this is not a same-setting performance decline. Some v2 values conflict internally: its BEV designation accuracy is 0.662 in Table 2 but 0.5497 in Table 7-2.

T1.justification: Neither version presents theoretical propositions or proofs. The descriptions of nearest-neighbor matching, coordinate normalization, capped RMSE, and Fréchet-distance evaluation remain substantively unchanged; the additional cross-view tasks reuse existing metrics.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion revise the contribution to eight tasks, 3,040 cases, and 20 evaluated models. Joint cross-view evaluation broadens the benchmark's stated scope, and the abstract specifies five Chinese cities. The central contribution and claim of inadequate fine-grained urban spatial reasoning remain intact.

C2.justification: v2 adds interpretations concerning cross-view alignment and fine-tuning benefits, expands the final error taxonomy to include cross-view consistency and structured-output failures, and cautions against definitive rankings on small splits. It also states geographic and deployment boundaries and imagery-update limitations. Section 4.2 narrows the lane-designation baseline claim from no models outperforming it to most models failing to do so.

D1.justification: v2 adds a benchmark code link and statements about data access, reconstruction instructions, provenance, consistency checks, evaluation scripts, and raw outputs. It also documents paired-image curation, cross-view prompts, unique image counts, and five expert auditors. These substantially expand disclosure, although fine-tuning hyperparameters and train/test allocation remain absent; linked resources were not independently verified.

R1.justification: v2 adds the Qwen3-VL technical-report citation and explicitly discusses UrbanMLLM in related work. UrbanMLLM was already cited in v1, so its updated publication information is not a newly added work. The benchmark comparison in Table 1 and overall research positioning remain largely unchanged.

P1.justification: Most section ordering, prose, original prompts, and detailed case narratives are retained. Local rewrites affect the abstract, quality-control description, and results discussion; new subsections organize uncertainty reporting and the expanded error summary. Author, affiliation, and acknowledgement text also changes.

P2.justification: The document changes from two-column to single-column formatting. Figure 2 gains a cross-view tier, Table 2 expands its model/task structure and loses its rank column, and three appendix tables are added. Most appendix example and failure-case figures move to the final pages, far from their associated text; robustness tables also lose relative-change annotations.

improvement.justification: v2 adds useful cross-view coverage, fine-tuning comparisons, uncertainty reporting, and reproducibility information that v1 lacked. However, the reduced test set and new training procedure are insufficiently specified, and new reporting conflicts materially affect conclusions: GPT-5-Mini's BEV designation accuracy differs between Tables 2 and 7-2. Some retained environmental interpretations also fail to track the revised results in Table 8-13. These gains and unresolved reliability problems prevent a confident judgment of net overall improvement.
